question: What is the revenue per active customer, counting only customers who have placed an order?
verdict_why: every axis an expectation of COMMIT requires passes

all 3 bound never-clauses are prose; none is machine-checkable, so there is nothing here a machine can decide

answer_sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(s.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_key), 2) AS "revenue per active customer"
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
JOIN (
  SELECT
    c.customer_key
  FROM contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
  LEFT JOIN contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS sl
    ON sl.customer_key = c.customer_key
  GROUP BY
    c.customer_key
  HAVING
    COUNT(DISTINCT sl.order_key) > 0
) AS b
  ON s.customer_key = b.customer_key

body.value: The one row returned carries one figure: 4,192.73 US dollars of net revenue per active customer. It is 218,814,471.66 of money actually charged, after discount, shared over the 52,189 people who have ever placed an order — each of whom placed 1 to 9 of the warehouse's 93,470 orders — covering every order date from 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, in the physical shops and the web shop together. WHAT IT IS NOT: not an annual rate. Ten years sit inside it, so it is lifetime-to-date spend per buying customer; the yearly equivalent is about 419. It excludes the 52,801 registered customers who have never bought — including them would halve it to 2,084.13. It is net of discount but not of refunds, returns or cancellations, because this bundle records none. In USD, which is the unit of the amounts whatever currency each sale was transacted in.

value: 218,814,471.66 of net_amount summed over all 223,974 rows of contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line — the whole sales fact, with no period and no channel predicate — divided by the 52,189 customers of contoso_served.dim_customer holding at least one distinct order_key. The restrictions I applied, and where each came from: (1) customers cut to those with at least one order, because the question says "active customer" and the document's reading of it is anyone who has ever ordered — this drops 52,801 of the 104,990 registered customers; (2) no channel filter, because store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel carries applies: subject and this question's subject is a measure, so the web shop's 86,790,054.13 is in alongside the shops' 132,024,417.53; (3) no period filter, by order.default.an_unscoped_question_covers_all_time, giving the full extent 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31; (4) net_amount rather than gross_amount, by net_revenue.default.revenue_means_net. Routing the revenue through the buyer population removed nothing — zero lines carry a customer_key absent from the register, so the numerator is the complete sales fact.

value.means: The one row returned carries one figure: 4,192.73 US dollars of net revenue per active customer. It is 218,814,471.66 of money actually charged, after discount, shared over the 52,189 people who have ever placed an order — each of whom placed 1 to 9 of the warehouse's 93,470 orders — covering every order date from 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, in the physical shops and the web shop together. WHAT IT IS NOT: not an annual rate. Ten years sit inside it, so it is lifetime-to-date spend per buying customer; the yearly equivalent is about 419. It excludes the 52,801 registered customers who have never bought — including them would halve it to 2,084.13. It is net of discount but not of refunds, returns or cancellations, because this bundle records none. In USD, which is the unit of the amounts whatever currency each sale was transacted in.
